---
id: create-capacity-plan
title: "Create a DRAFT CapacityPlan and compute its shortage"
description: "Evaluates the ProcessPath path_id against assigned_demand (orders) for the warehouse's location over [window_start, window_end): loads each step's ProcessCapacity, normalizes it with the WorkloadProfile factors supplied in the body (same shape and validation as GET /process-paths/{id}/capacity -- there is no WorkloadProfile persistence yet), and computes path_capacity (ORDER per HOUR), bottleneck_step, capacity_over_window (path_capacity x window hours) and shortage (max(0, assigned_demand - capacity_over_window), never negative). The window is both the plan's planning window AND the window every step's ProcessCapacity is looked up for: a registered window applies to a step when it COVERS [window_start, window_end), exactly as in GET /process-paths/{id}/capacity (docs/adr/0003). The plan stores its own requested window. site_id is REQUIRED: the canonical site (a facility-layout Site site_code, the same identifier its SiteCapabilityChanged event publishes) the plan is scoped to. It is a stated planning fact, never inferred from warehouse_id or location, and a blank or absent one is rejected with 422 missing-required-field. assigned_demand is OPTIONAL (docs/adr/0004). An explicit value (including 0) is used exactly as stated and the plan's demand_source is 'request'. When it is OMITTED the demand defaults to the number of orders the local read model -- fed by order-management's published OrderAllocated / OrderPartiallyAllocated events, never by a live call -- expects at `location` in [window_start, window_end) (see GET /demand), the plan's demand_source is 'orders', and assigned_demand in the response is that figure. When the read model has no order for that location and window the request is rejected with 422 missing-assigned-demand: absence never silently means zero demand. demand_source (docs/adr/0024) may name the source instead: 'forecast' derives assigned_demand from the workload forecast of (site_id, forecast_path_id, default path_id) -- the units of the buckets whose cpt is in the window over units_per_order, rounded up to orders -- and the plan returns forecast_path_id. labour_requirement (docs/adr/0022) states, per path step, the labour its demand requires: tasks x the standard seconds of the step's task type, read from the local copy of labor-performance's labour standards (fed by its LaborStandardDefined / LaborStandardRevised events, never by a live call) for the plan's site at window_start. The optional tasks_per_order map counts a step's tasks; a step without a standard or without a task count is known false with a reason. It is informational: the shortage, the bottleneck and every published event are unchanged by it. The plan is saved and its CapacityPlanCreated event is queued in the transactional outbox in ONE database transaction."

<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Create a DRAFT CapacityPlan and compute its shortage"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/capacity-plans"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



Evaluates the ProcessPath path_id against assigned_demand (orders) for the warehouse's location over [window_start, window_end): loads each step's ProcessCapacity, normalizes it with the WorkloadProfile factors supplied in the body (same shape and validation as GET /process-paths/\{id\}/capacity -- there is no WorkloadProfile persistence yet), and computes path_capacity (ORDER per HOUR), bottleneck_step, capacity_over_window (path_capacity x window hours) and shortage (max(0, assigned_demand - capacity_over_window), never negative). The window is both the plan's planning window AND the window every step's ProcessCapacity is looked up for: a registered window applies to a step when it COVERS [window_start, window_end), exactly as in GET /process-paths/\{id\}/capacity (docs/adr/0003). The plan stores its own requested window. site_id is REQUIRED: the canonical site (a facility-layout Site site_code, the same identifier its SiteCapabilityChanged event publishes) the plan is scoped to. It is a stated planning fact, never inferred from warehouse_id or location, and a blank or absent one is rejected with 422 missing-required-field. assigned_demand is OPTIONAL (docs/adr/0004). An explicit value (including 0) is used exactly as stated and the plan's demand_source is "request". When it is OMITTED the demand defaults to the number of orders the local read model -- fed by order-management's published OrderAllocated / OrderPartiallyAllocated events, never by a live call -- expects at `location` in [window_start, window_end) (see GET /demand), the plan's demand_source is "orders", and assigned_demand in the response is that figure. When the read model has no order for that location and window the request is rejected with 422 missing-assigned-demand: absence never silently means zero demand. demand_source (docs/adr/0024) may name the source instead: "forecast" derives assigned_demand from the workload forecast of (site_id, forecast_path_id, default path_id) -- the units of the buckets whose cpt is in the window over units_per_order, rounded up to orders -- and the plan returns forecast_path_id. labour_requirement (docs/adr/0022) states, per path step, the labour its demand requires: tasks x the standard seconds of the step's task type, read from the local copy of labor-performance's labour standards (fed by its LaborStandardDefined / LaborStandardRevised events, never by a live call) for the plan's site at window_start. The optional tasks_per_order map counts a step's tasks; a step without a standard or without a task count is known false with a reason. It is informational: the shortage, the bottleneck and every published event are unchanged by it. The plan is saved and its CapacityPlanCreated event is queued in the transactional outbox in ONE database transaction.

A missing key is 400 idempotency-key-required, a malformed one 400 idempotency-key-invalid; the same key with a different method, path or body is 409 idempotency-key-reused; the same key with the same request replays the stored answer with Idempotency-Replayed: true. Which answers a retry replays is the problem type's replay class (ADR 0026): FINAL refusals and every 2xx are stored and replayed; a RETRYABLE refusal (version-conflict, process-path-not-found, missing-step-capacity, missing-assigned-demand, ...) commits nothing, is not stored and RELEASES the key, so a retry under the same key executes again and a different body under it is a new request.\n","schema":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":128}}]}
